text:
maria: Heads-up — saw a slow memory climb on prod-kv (shard-7) around 03:12 UTC, spikes correlate with long-seq requests. opening follow-ups here.
jonathan: thanks. is this similar to last month's sticky residency incident? https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RI-2561
maria: similar surface but different shape: steady small growth vs the big jumps we saw before. suspect fragmentation + retention.
lee: uploaded alloc profiles: gs://redwood/prof/persist/2472000000.tar.gz (pv-202703). will run diff next.
sam_k: i'll schedule a heap-scan job during the quiet window tonight (02:00-04:00 UTC).
ops-bot: deploy ":canary-v5.3" completed at 2472000100 — canary 2/5 active.
maria: proposed owners & deadlines: 1) profiling — @lee — full per-shard heap scan + flamegraphs — target Fri EOD. 2) softlimits/guards — @jonathan — proto + PR by Tue. 3) GC/compact policy experiments — @alex — canary tests by Wed. 4) quick pooling patch — @sam_k + lee — PR by tomorrow morning.
jonathan: ack. need perf harness details and a small benchmark for eviction impact. can someone paste the harness link?
alex: i'll wire up compact-every-5m experiment on canary shards and add 'residency' gauge. will post graphs.
lee: initial heap-scan shows a lot of small allocs attributed to persist.IndexEntry retaining buffers. snippet: 
``
name: IndexEntry
size: ~48 bytes
alloc stack: encoder.go:132 -> persist.go:78 -> cache.go:49
```
maria: that aligns with slow growth. if encoder holds buffers, pooled buffers might cut steady leakage. can we try a minimal pooling change?
sam_k: pooling patch low-risk. i'll pair with lee for a quick PR and perf test. aiming for a canary-ready PR by 12:00 UTC tomorrow.
jonathan: softlimit plan: implement soft-residency limit per-shard (percentile-based), eviction bump on threshold, fallback to lower-capacity model. rollout plan: canary -> 10% -> 50% -> full; fail if OOM rate >0.5% within 30m.
maria: added tracking sheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/abc123 — filled owners + dates.
alex: recurring pattern note: spikes most visible when average seq_len >1024 and concurrent clients >200. suggests shard-specific thresholds rather than global.
maria: good call. add a row to sheet for seq_len trigger and a TODO to tune per-shard.
jonathan: created Jira RI-2719 for softlimit work and RI-2720 for eviction instrumentation.
ops-bot: Jira RI-2719 assigned to jonathan, due 2027-03-29.
lee: will post flamegraphs and per-shard diffs here when scans finish.
sam_k: started pooling PR branch: feat/pool-indexentry — pairing with lee shortly. :thumbsup:
maria: weekly follow-up: Thu 10am PT sync to close actions and validate no regression. i'll update the postmortem with owners/timelines and link incident notes. cc @sam_k @lee @jonathan
jonathan: will add benchmark notes to the PR and schedule perf run after canary.
lee: quick note — if pooling reduces allocation but not residency, we'll pivot to aggressive compacting and a short-term eviction ramp.
maria: thanks everyone. i'll file a short customer-impact blurb for support and update stakeholders after the Thu sync.
